To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proved a general theorem on the spectral convexity of attractive fermions in arbitrary dimensions.

(a) the spectral function of attractive 2N fermions is convex with respect to the particle number; (b) this convexity is a consequence of a negative definite Fourier transform of the interaction potential; (c) the convexity result implies clustering of the ground state.
the ground state of a system of attractive SU(2 N)-symmetric fermions with a negative definite Fourier transform of the two-body interaction potential is a 2 N-particle clustering state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ground state properties of fermionic systems with attractive SU(2)-invariant interactions.
the ground state properties of many-body fermionic systems.
the study of the properties of the many-body Hamiltonian of a quantum system of particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ground state of the system is in a clustering phase, and that the ground state energy of a system of fermions with a two-body SU(2N )-symmetric interaction is convex with respect to the particle number.
the SU(2N), N=1 and N=2, symmetry is a sufficient condition to prove that the ground state of a system of fermions is in a phase of clustering.
the ground state of a 2N-degenerate Fermi system is a 2N-clustered state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the attractive SU(2) model has a unique ground state and that the ground state energy is a convex function of particle number, while for SU(3) and SU(4) the ground state is not unique and the ground state energy may have a concave region.
we have proved that a large class of fermionic systems with attractive SU(2)N invariant interactions are in a clustering phase.

we show that the ground states of fermions in the attractive SU(2)N potential have a tendency to cluster into N-particle clusters, which are either bosonic (N=1,3,...), or fermionic (N=2,4,...) depending on the number of components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ground state of a large class of fermionic systems is a cluster of 2N fermions, with no other fermions nearby.
the attractive interactions that are known to drive the clustering in light nuclei are sufficient to drive clustering in neutron stars.
the attractive SU(2)-symmetric interaction has a universal tendency towards clustering in the ground state, which is independent of the details of the external potential.
